# anonymized: invented text with the same problem shape as a real prompt that stopped early (cause A: ends in a question, no permission to implement)

Bug: the background worker's "done" notification silently never reaches an open session - measured, not theoretical.
The project notes already flag this as unproven: "the notify step has never been tested against a live session; it may only append a line to the log." I just measured it. It fails.

Repro, this run: `tool run --plan plan.json --detach --notify <session-id>`. The worker ran, paused after two retries, and the worker log shows `NOTIFY <session-id> (detached)` with the right id. The notify log says the message was sent. My open session never saw it.

Root cause, as I understand it: the notify step starts a brand-new detached process that resumes the session headlessly. That is not the same channel as a tracked background task finishing, which is the only thing that wakes an open session.

My concern as the user, not just the bug: we moved to detached mode so an accidental "stop all agents" could not kill the worker mid-run. But the tracked mode gave us visibility, and we lost it.

What I need from you: a design that gives me both - survives an accidental kill AND gives me live visibility and a reliable wake. Options I can imagine, tell me which is right or propose better:

1. Go back to tracked background tasks, plus protection against the kill gesture that stopped two runs last time.
2. Keep detached mode, make the wake provably land in a live session, and add a way to see the worker is alive.
3. Something else - a hybrid, a heartbeat, whatever actually solves both.

Not resuming any run until this is resolved.
